title: Check yourself: Getting JSON: schemas, structured outputs and strict tools

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team wants every reply from Claude Sonnet 5.5 to be a record in a fixed JSON shape. What does the documentation recommend?

options.text: A tool choice of any, so that some tool is always called
options.says: Ruled out because `any` is one of the values that "return a 400 error" on this model.

options.text: A forced tool whose schema is the record, chosen with the name field
options.says: Ruled out because `any` and `tool` "return a 400 error" on Claude Sonnet 5.5.

options.text: A prompt that shows the record and asks the model to copy the shape
options.says: Ruled out because a prompt gives "no guarantee; the program must parse defensively".

options.text: Structured outputs with the schema in the output configuration
options.says: The page says to use structured outputs "when you need a response in a fixed JSON shape".

origin.section: Forced tools are not always available

questions.stem: The schema says a field named `total` has a `minimum` of 0, and the request is sent with that schema unchanged. What happens?

options.text: It fails with a 400 error that comes with details of the unsupported item
options.says: The page says "If you use an unsupported feature, you'll receive a 400 error with details."

options.text: The reply is checked against the limit and retried for the caller
options.says: Ruled out because "a helper that validates responses still enforces every constraint in your code", so the check is the program's job.

options.text: The limit is read as a hint and the call goes on as usual
options.says: Ruled out because "If you use an unsupported feature" the outcome is an error, with no hint read.

options.text: The constraint is applied only when the field is a whole number
options.says: Ruled out because the numerical constraints are listed as unsupported with no exception: "Numerical constraints (such as `minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`)".

questions.stem: A reply arrives with a 200 status and `stop_reason` of `refusal`. What should the program assume about the body?

options.text: It becomes whole once the call is repeated with more tokens
options.says: Ruled out because the remedy of more tokens belongs to `max_tokens`: "Retry with a higher `max_tokens` value to get the complete structured output."

options.text: It keeps the shape, because the status code says success
options.says: Ruled out because a refusal has "a 200 status code and billed tokens" and still breaks the shape.

options.text: The model's decline takes the place of the promised shape
options.says: The page says "The output may not match your schema because the refusal message takes precedence over schema constraints."

options.text: It is always an empty object, which signals the refusal
options.says: Ruled out because the page names no such body, only that the output "may not match your schema".

origin.section: Two replies that do not follow the schema
